reports.summary: Yemeni government forces shoot down Houthi drone in Taiz
reports.text: TAIZ — Yemeni government forces shot down a Houthi drone carrying a mortar shell in the Kadha front west of Taiz governorate.

reports.summary: Yemeni army secures positions in Taiz amid ongoing clashes
reports.text: Yemeni government forces secured positions on Mount Numan in Jabal Habashi, west of Taiz, and targeted Houthi reinforcements amid ongoing clashes in the western and southwestern fronts of the governorate.

reports.summary: Yemeni government forces shell Houthi military positions in Marib
reports.text: MARIB — Yemeni government forces targeted Houthi military positions in Marib with artillery, while warplanes launched an attack on the Jabal Hilan mountain range.

reports.summary: Armed forces drone strikes Houthi positions in Hajjah
reports.text: HAJJAH — The armed forces announced that drone aircraft from the Fifth Military Region targeted Houthi fortifications, gatherings, and barracks in combat fronts across Hajjah governorate.

reports.summary: Clashes renew between Houthi forces and government forces in Taiz and Lahj
reports.text: TAIZ — Back-and-forth clashes broke out between Houthi forces and government forces in several areas of Taiz, while fighting renewed on the Kahbub front in Lahj governorate.

reports.summary: Houthi health ministry reports casualties in Jawf airstrikes
reports.text: AL-JAWF — The health ministry in the unrecognised Houthi administration announced that four people were killed and three others working in the telecommunications sector were injured by air strikes hitting telecommunications towers in Khabb wa al-Sha'af district in Jawf governorate.

reports.summary: Residents of al-Turban send food convoy to government fighters in Taiz
reports.text: TAIZ — Residents of al-Turban, the center of al-Shamayatin district in Taiz governorate, sent a food convoy named "Wafa convoy" to support government forces stationed on the western fronts of the governorate.

reports.summary: Trump: decided against US strikes on the Houthis in Yemen
reports.text: Trump decided against launching US strikes against the Houthis in Yemen after reversing course following preparations by the Department of Defence. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman urged him to intervene, prompting Trump to order the strikes before changing his mind.

reports.summary: Drone attack on camp in Aden
reports.text: People were killed and wounded after a booby-trapped drone launched by Houthi forces targeted a camp in Aden. Local sources said the drone struck Camp "al-Jawiyah previously" in the Jaulah area.

reports.summary: Trump administration officials: Trump decided against ordering air strikes on Yemen
reports.text: Trump administration officials said Trump decided against ordering air strikes on Yemen at present, after briefly asking the Pentagon to prepare for strikes following a personal appeal from Mohammed bin Salman on Thursday. Most of Trump's inner circle opposed opening another front in the war.

reports.summary: Clashes reported in al-Turbah without Houthi control
reports.text: Clashes were reported in al-Turbah in Taiz without any advance or control by Houthi forces.

reports.summary: Rocket launch reported from Sanaa
reports.text: A rocket launch operation was reported originating from Sanaa.

reports.summary: Saree: Saudi warplanes carried out 28 air strikes in 24 hours
reports.text: Saree said Saudi war planes carried out 28 air strikes in the past 24 hours using F15 and Typhoon aircraft that took off from Khamis Mushait and Taif bases, targeting Taiz, Al-Jawf and Marib governorates, bringing the total number of strikes since the start of the Saudi escalation to 760 air strikes.

reports.summary: Saree: Saudi warplanes carried out 28 air strikes in 24 hours

reports.summary: al-Arada: Houthi advance toward Bab al-Mandab raises risks to navigation
reports.text: Sultan al-Arada, member of the Presidential Leadership Council, warned of military developments, stating that Houthi forces reaching strategic areas toward Bab al-Mandab increase risks to international navigation and trade security.

reports.summary: al-Mashat: UN seat for Yemen is vacant and representative speaks for Saudi Arabia
reports.text: Mahdi al-Mashat stated that Yemen's seat in the United Nations and representation at the annual General Assembly meeting are vacant, asserting that anyone claiming the status represents the voice of Saudi Arabia rather than Yemen.

reports.summary: al-Mashat: Saudi Arabia resorted to procrastination during truce
reports.text: Mahdi al-Mashat stated that during the truce, the Saudi regime was invited to implement the road map and complete peace, but instead chose procrastination and tightened its blockade.

reports.summary: al-Mashat: Coastal operations carried out to enforce Yemeni sovereignty
reports.text: Mahdi al-Mashat stated that actions taken by Yemeni armed forces in coastal areas were a national operation to enforce Yemeni sovereignty and expel Saudi mobilizations.

reports.summary: al-Mashat: We acknowledge public steadfastness despite halted salaries
reports.text: Mahdi al-Mashat acknowledged the public's endurance regarding cut salaries, dried-up resources, and targeted currency, while the 21 September revolution continues local production.

reports.summary: al-Mashat: We deprecate false Saudi claims of targeting Mecca
reports.text: Mahdi al-Mashat rejected what he termed false Saudi fabrications regarding the army targeting Mecca, asserting that the army's nobility is known to the world.

reports.summary: al-Mashat: Real and just peace remains our strategic choice
reports.text: Mahdi al-Mashat stated that true and just peace has been and will remain a strategic choice, noting that peace with Yemen is the least costly path.

reports.summary: Fierce clashes reported in Taiz fronts
reports.text: TAIZ — Fierce clashes erupted between Saudi-backed forces and Ansar Allah in the fronts of Taiz as forces attempted to prevent advances towards strategic mountains.

reports.summary: Yemeni military reports airstrikes on Taiz and Mokha
reports.text: TAIZ — Houthi supply routes and positions came under airstrikes in Taiz and Mokha, according to the Yemeni military.

reports.summary: Yemeni forces advance toward Al-Turbah in Taiz
reports.text: Yemeni forces advanced toward Al-Turbah, bringing them around 35 kilometers from the town and threatening the final major supply route for forces backed by Saudi Arabia connecting Taiz and Aden.

reports.summary: Saudi government installs new sirens in Taif
reports.text: TAIF — The Saudi government installed new warning sirens in the city of Taif, which houses King Fahd Air Base.

reports.summary: Southern forces thwart Houthi night attack in Yafah
reports.text: YAFA — Southern forces thwarted a large nighttime Houthi attack and infiltration attempt across the fronts of the Yafah axis, sparking intense clashes with heavy and medium weapons.

reports.summary: Government forces claim they retook Jabal Numan and repelled attacks at Al-Shamayatayn and Jabal Habashi

reports.summary: Yemeni transport ministry reports 316 ships crossed Bab al-Mandab
reports.text: A transport ministry source stated that 316 ships crossed the Bab al-Mandab strait between September 10 and 18, with a daily average of about 35 ships.

reports.summary: Sanaa forces advance in Taiz and Lahj amid clashes and air strikes
reports.text: AL-ALQAMAH — Sanaa forces advanced in the Shamaiteen district of Taiz, seizing tabat al-Jorif and the villages of al-Makhshab, Sharira and al-Qahfa. Saudi jets launched air strikes on the vicinity of marafq al-Zikrah, al-Damnah and al-Rahidah in Taiz governorate, while clashes continued in Lahj governorate.

reports.summary: Houthi forces blow up homes of Tihama forces commanders
reports.text: Houthi forces carried out a wave of bombings targeting homes of military and prominent commanders of the Tihama forces in the Western Coast, destroying them completely.

reports.summary: Yemeni armed forces destroy Houthi military vehicle in Taiz
reports.text: Clashes between the armed forces and Houthi forces in the western fronts of Taiz governorate resulted in armed forces directly targeting a Houthi military vehicle in Jabal Habashi district.

reports.summary: Yemeni forces take control of Al-Khabl area in Al-Alqamah front
reports.text: Yemeni forces took control of Al-Khabl area, the center of Al-Alqamah, following fierce battles on the Al-Alqamah-Sharirah front.

reports.summary: Al-Maliki: Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed ballistic missile over Riyadh
reports.text: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Houthis toward Riyadh, and thwarted attempted attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Bisha, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu.

reports.summary: Saudi authorities intercept ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh
reports.text: RIYADH — Saudi authorities reported shooting down a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh on Saturday, as Houthi militants in Yemen said they carried out drone and ballistic missile attacks on the Saudi capital and Red Sea energy sites.

reports.summary: Al-Maliki: Saudi air defense forces intercepted Houthi missile targeting Riyadh
reports.text: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki stated that Royal Saudi Air Defense Forces intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward Riyadh, and thwarted attempted Houthi attacks on Baysh, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu.

reports.summary: Yemeni military command reports 13 personnel killed in clashes

reports.text: Southern Giants Brigades forces carried out artillery and drone strikes targeting Houthi vehicles, fortifications, and trenches in the Al-Bayda front.

reports.text: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia confirmed that air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh. The Saudi-led coalition added that Houthi attacks targeting civilian infrastructure in Yanbu, Taif, Baysh, and Farasan were also thwarted.

reports.text: HODEIDAH — Yemeni government forces engaged in clashes with Houthi fighters across the Hodeidah and Dhale fronts, while also responding to sudden attacks and armed Houthi movements in central and northern fronts.

reports.text: RIYADH — The United States warned that hostilities could escalate rapidly after a missile attack targeted Riyadh, causing a fire in a fuel tank near the airport. The White House gave no explanation for President Donald Trump cutting short a weekend at Camp David.

reports.text: RIYADH — Residents in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh received the all-clear after air raid alerts were issued and explosions were reported in the capital. It was the first time alerts have been issued in Riyadh since the Houthis increased their attacks.

reports.text: KAHBUB — Clashes between the Giants Brigades and Houthi forces in Bab al-Mandab and Kahbub on 19 September. Full detail is at the source link.

reports.summary: Yemeni armed forces recapture positions in southwest Taiz
reports.text: The Yemeni armed forces recaptured positions in southwest Taiz, including Mount al-Shuhada overlooking Wadi al-Ghail in al-Wazi'iyah. Military aircraft carried out air strikes on Houthi positions around the Palace roundabout east of Taiz city.

reports.text: TAIZ — Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson Saree stated that Saudi warplanes launched 26 air strikes on Taiz over 24 hours, and 300 total strikes over the week across Taiz, Hajjah, Marib, al-Jawf, al-Bayda, Amran, Lahj, Hodeidah, and Saada, taking off from Khamis Mushait and Taif bases.

reports.summary: Clashes in Marib's Al-Wadi district as Houthi forces attack the contact lines
reports.text: MARIB — Fighting broke out in the Al-Wadi district of Marib between security forces and armed tribesmen, leaving two dead, alongside a Houthi offensive on several axes in the governorate, including fire on the supply road at Al-Hazmah. Almashhad carried the account.

reports.summary: Drone strikes around Sanaa, in a claimed first combat use of the SKYWASP
reports.text: SANAA — Explosions were heard at dawn around Sanaa and in the nearby hills. A military source attributed the sorties to strikes on air defences, arms depots and missile and drone sites, and an analyst identified the weapon as the SKYWASP drone. There is no official government confirmation of the drone's identity. Almashhad and Sheba Intelligence carried the account.

reports.summary: Clashes and strikes in Taiz leave over 90 Houthi dead or wounded
reports.text: AL-WAZI'IYAH — Clashes and air strikes in the Al-Waziyah district of Taiz resulted in 30 Houthi fighters killed and over 60 others injured, according to a military source. The operations also destroyed six combat vehicles and two tanks.

reports.summary: More than 112,000 displaced by the fighting in Yemen, with about 3,000 fleeing by boat to Djibouti
reports.text: More than 112,000 people have been displaced inside Yemen in two weeks and about 3,000 have crossed by boat to Djibouti, the United Nations said. UNHCR said more than 2,400 arrived in the past week, most of them women, children and older people. Djibouti, a country of about a million people already hosting some 36,000 refugees, is preparing for up to 10,000. About 2,000 of the displaced are pregnant women, and around 22 million people in Yemen need assistance. The displacement widened after the Houthi seizure of the Red Sea coast.

reports.summary: Yemeni armed forces target Houthi gatherings in Marib with drones
reports.text: MARIB — The Yemeni armed forces carried out drone attacks targeting Houthi gatherings in the northern fronts of Marib. Meanwhile, artillery units destroyed nine Houthi combat vehicles in the western fronts.

reports.summary: Yemeni government forces repel Houthi attack and advance in Taiz
reports.text: TAIZ — Yemeni government forces repelled a Houthi attack in the Kadha front west of Taiz and recaptured positions in Jabal al-Shuhada in the Al-Waziyah district.

reports.summary: Yemeni army recaptures positions and shoots down drone in Taiz
reports.text: TAIZ — Yemeni army forces recaptured positions in the Kadha area of Al-Ma'afir district and the Al-Waziyah district in Taiz following clashes with Houthi forces, while also shooting down a drone.

reports.summary: UNHCR counts about 3,000 arrivals in Djibouti in under a week, while WHO finds only 60% of 5,415 Yemeni health facilities fully functioning
reports.text: Sandrine Desamours, the UNHCR representative in Djibouti, told a briefing at the Palais des Nations that about 3,000 people had crossed Bab al-Mandab in small boats in under a week, landing at Obock, Khor Angar, Moulhoule and Godoria. More than half were women and children, and some were families displaced for a second time since 2015. The Markazi refugee village, with capacity for 5,000, was already hosting more than 2,700 Yemenis and 1,500 Eritreans, with about 270 more staying with host families. The Djiboutian government is preparing for up to 10,000. UNHCR's Djibouti operation is 15% funded, short about $5.1 million, and its Yemen operation 18% funded, needing a further $14 million for shelter and site management. WHO spokesman Tarik Jasarevic said only 60% of 5,415 health facilities assessed in Yemen were fully functioning. Reported by UNHCR, WHO and TRT World.

reports.summary: Yemeni army air strikes target Houthi positions in Taiz
reports.text: TAIZ — Military warplanes of the army launched air strikes on Houthi positions and gatherings around the Palace Roundabout east of Taiz.

reports.summary: Guardian reports an internal inquiry on the anti-Houthi side into the collapse of the west coast, with claims that some 30,000 fighters withdrew and suspicions of bribery
reports.text: A bitter inquiry has opened on the anti-Houthi side into the collapse of what was meant to be a decisive push on Sanaa and instead became a rout. More than 15 brigades were defeated as the entire west coast fell to the Houthis. Yemeni politicians say billions of dollars were offered to persuade forces on the coast to abandon their positions, and estimate that some 30,000 fighters withdrew. Tawakkol Karman called for an investigation, and a resident of Mocha described the 10 September withdrawal as a betrayal. The Guardian reported the account.

reports.summary: UKMTO reports no new attack on shipping in the Red Sea, with the threat still focused on Saudi-linked vessels after the fall of Mocha and Mayun
reports.text: UKMTO's seventh voluntary reporting area review recorded 110 warnings and 17 advisories since the start of the year, and 100 incidents connected to the Iran-US war. No new attack was logged in the Red Sea or at Bab al-Mandab on 18 September, and the most recent incidents on the list were in the Strait of Hormuz on 14 and 15 September. The official note says the threat to shipping is in line with the declared embargo on Saudi-linked vessels, and that six deaths have been reported to UKMTO since the embargo was announced on 22 July. The fall of Mocha reflects greater Houthi control along stretches of the Red Sea coast. JMIC continues to rate the southern Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab as high threat. This is a maritime status update, not a change of ground control.

reports.summary: Government forces retake positions from Houthi fighters in Al-Wazi'iyah
reports.text: Government forces and local tribal forces recaptured sites from Houthi forces in Al-Wazi'iyah district in Taiz governorate, including Mount Al-Bazlah.

reports.source: Saudi Gazette · Al Arabiya · Saudi MoD
reports.summary: Saudi-led defensive naval coalition reaches initial operational capability, with 41 states at a planning session in Jeddah
reports.text: The Saudi-led multinational defensive naval coalition held its fourth planning session at Western Fleet headquarters in Jeddah, attended by 154 naval commanders, planners, ambassadors and European Union representatives from 41 states, the Saudi defence ministry said. The coalition has reached initial operational capability and moved from formation to integrating capabilities, operational readiness and a physical presence in the maritime area it covers, with 28 liaison officers. Its stated aim is to protect freedom of navigation, sea lanes and straits under international law. No deployment timetable was given, the 41 states were not named, and the statement makes no explicit reference to Yemen or Bab al-Mandab. This is a diplomatic announcement, not a change of control.

reports.summary: Three children reported killed by a Houthi shell on the village of Al-Tarirah in Al-Wazi'iyah, with the names published
reports.text: Three children were killed in the village of Al-Tarirah in Al-Wazi'iyah district in western Taiz, in what local sources describe as Houthi shelling of a residential area. The names published were Nur al-Din Yaqub Abduh al-Tharafi, about four; Asawar Fahd Mohammed Ghanim al-Tharafi, 14; and Tala Mohammed Ahmed al-Tharafi, about two. The sources link the incident to the escalation in western Taiz and to shelling of inhabited areas. An earlier Al Jazeera and AFP report on 17 September carried a separate Houthi media claim blaming government and coalition forces for the same village, leaving the attribution contested. Almashhad and Saba carried the accounts.

reports.summary: Al Jazeera reports US officials met the Houthis in Muscat, where the Houthis pledged to spare American vessels and strike only Saudi-linked ships
reports.text: US officials met Houthi representatives at the US embassy in Muscat over the weekend, after the Houthi seizure of the coast and the islands. The Houthis gave an assurance that they do not intend to attack American vessels in the Red Sea and that restrictions would apply only to ships with a Saudi connection. Al Jazeera's reading is that Washington, already stretched by the war with Iran, would rather not open a front in Yemen.

reports.summary: Ali Bk relays Saree's claim that Islamic State-style Saudi attempts were foiled in Sanaa and will not go unanswered
reports.text: Houthi forces spokesman Yahya Saree said criminal attempts in the capital Sanaa carried out by Saudi forces, which he described as coloured by Islamic State methods, had been foiled and would not go unanswered. No operational detail was given and there is no independent confirmation; this is recorded as a spokesman's claim. Ali Bk carried the statement.

reports.summary: Ali Bk reports a Saudi A330 tanker and a Saab 2000 early-warning aircraft flying south towards Yemen
reports.text: A Saudi A330 tanker aircraft and a Saab 2000 early-warning aircraft were observed flying south towards Yemen in support of detection work, according to a Telegram post by Ali Bk. This is an air-tracking claim with no Saudi confirmation.

reports.summary: Government forces in western Taiz claim they repelled a Houthi attack at Al-Kadha, shot down two drones and killed 15 fighters
reports.text: Government forces and the Popular Resistance in western Taiz say they foiled a Houthi attack on the Al-Kadha front, shot down two Houthi drones before they reached their targets and killed 15 of the attackers. According to the same account, some bodies were left in the hills after the attackers withdrew. The source says the front remained in the defenders' hands and that alert levels are unchanged. This is a government and local claim only, with no independent verification. Almashhad carried the account.

reports.summary: Reuters at the Al-Birin camp in Taiz finds families fleeing barefoot after shelling, with aid agencies counting about 115,000 people on the move since the Houthi advance
reports.text: Rawya Hassan and her family fled barefoot from shelling around the camp where they had been sheltering, leaving livestock and belongings behind. The family had already been displaced once before. Aid agencies report about 115,000 people on the move since the Houthi advance, and the IOM counts at least 112,000 internally displaced in two weeks, with about 3,000 crossing to Djibouti in overloaded boats. Reuters reported from the Al-Birin camp in Taiz.

reports.summary: Heavy fighting reported on the Aghbara, Sharirah, Al-Alqamah, Al-Mansurah and Al-Bukrah fronts in western Taiz
reports.text: Violent clashes between Houthi forces and Saudi-aligned forces were reported on the Aghbara, Sharirah, Al-Alqamah, Al-Mansurah and Al-Bukrah fronts, the districts that link Taiz to the coast at Mocha. The account comes from an Iraqi-based channel and there is no independent confirmation of a decisive outcome. Ali Bk carried the post.

Al-Subayhah tribesmen in Lahj say they fought a ground engagement at Al-Bazilah, a position on the front facing Houthi forces in the Al-Aghbara area of Al-Mudaribah district, then took the position and are continuing to sweep the surroundings. According to the same account, Houthi forces suffered losses in men and equipment. This is a tribal and local claim only, with no independent verification. It is a different location from Aghbara at the edge of Al-Wazi'iyah in western Taiz. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Al-Subayhah tribes claim they seized the Al-Bazilah position in Lahj after a battle with Houthi forces

reports.text: The government army says it shot down a Houthi one-way attack drone on the western front in Taiz before it reached its target, after air defences tracked it in flight towards their positions. The same source reports a rise in one-way attack and reconnaissance drones on the Taiz fronts in recent days. This is a government claim, with no independent verification. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Government army in western Taiz claims it shot down a Houthi one-way attack drone before it reached its target

reports.text: The African Union Commission condemned Houthi attacks on civilian targets and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia and warned against escalation in the Red Sea and any threat to freedom of navigation at Bab al-Mandab. It said it was concerned by reports of attempts to strike Mecca and holy sites, and stressed that insecurity in the Red Sea and the strait is a strategic matter for the Horn of Africa and the littoral states. Almashhad carried the statement.
reports.summary: African Union Commission condemns Houthi attacks on civilian and economic targets in Saudi Arabia and warns of escalation
Crisis Group urges an urgent pause in Yemen, proposing a freeze of the front lines brokered in Oman
reports.text: In a statement headed Closing the new front in Yemen, the International Crisis Group said government forces lost Mocha on 11 September along with part of the defensive belt running from southern Hodeidah through western Taiz to Bab al-Mandab, giving the Houthis a better firing position against Saudi Arabia and against shipping. Its immediate recommendation is a pause, with Oman using its channels to freeze positions: the Houthis halting escalation inside Yemen, particularly around Taiz, and against Saudi Arabia, while Saudi Arabia and the government stop operations. ICG notes a fragmented command on the anti-Houthi side, spanning the National Resistance, the Giants Brigades, the Homeland Shield forces and the Taiz axis, with no single integrated army, and a two-straits problem for Saudi Arabia at Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab. It puts Saudi crude moving through the strait at more than 3.5 million barrels a day in early July, falling to almost nothing in August.

Mass gatherings were held in Al-Sabeen Square in Sanaa and in central squares across the governorates, under the banner of support for the armed forces, a siege-for-siege formula and rejection of what organisers called the false claim of a strike on Mecca, following a call by Abdul Malik al-Houthi the previous day. The confirmation that the rallies took place comes from an aligned outlet, with no independent crowd estimate. Al-Manar carried the account.
reports.summary: Unspecified reports from Sanaa and the surrounding governorates
Al Jazeera reports fighting in Taiz, Lahj and Marib, with the Homeland Shield forces claiming an attack blocked at Kahbub and the Giants Brigades claiming a drone downed at Rajum
reports.text: Fighting is concentrated in Taiz, Lahj and Marib, alongside dozens of sorties against Houthi positions. On the Kahbub front in Lahj, facing Bab al-Mandab, the Homeland Shield forces say they broke up a Houthi attack after more than three hours, repulsing it three times and forcing a withdrawal with losses in men and vehicles, without giving figures. The Giants Brigades say they shot down a Houthi Rajum drone before it reached its target, hit a troop concentration killing three, and destroyed four vehicles with their occupants. In western Taiz, around Al-Wazi'iyah and the Al-Dharifah junction, the army media centre repeats its 24-hour claim of 30 Houthi fighters killed and 60 wounded along with six vehicles and two tanks — the same framing already reported on 17 September, not new confirmation. Colonel Majed al-Nuzayli said government aircraft struck supply lines and positions in Taiz and Mocha. In western Marib, artillery and snipers are claimed to have burned out a Houthi crew and destroyed a 106mm gun. The Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of 37 sorties in 24 hours over Taiz and Hajjah. All of these are one-sided claims, with no independent verification and no confirmed change of control at Kahbub itself. Al Jazeera carried the round-up.

reports.summary: Houthi drone strike kills three children in Taiz
reports.text: AL-WAZI'IYAH — A Houthi drone strike targeted the village of Al-Tarirah in Al-Wazi'iyah district, killing three children and injuring others.

reports.summary: Houthi pressure on Saudi oil exports builds, with fire on facilities and tankers and world prices rising
reports.text: The Houthi seizure of the Red Sea coast and the strait has renewed pressure on Saudi oil exports, with fire directed at facilities and tankers, a fall in tanker traffic through Bab al-Mandab and an effect on world fuel prices. The Houthis say they are attacking only vessels with a Saudi connection. NPR reported the account.

A government military source described retaking Bab al-Mandab and the west coast as a top priority that will not be delayed. The source says two new artillery systems were brought to the fronts the previous day: Jahannam, a rocket launcher with a range of about 37km, and Al-Aqrab, a precision gun with a range of about 40km, both cued by drones and paired with a field detection system called MAVEN, firing within less than a minute of drone designation as a complement to air strikes. This is a one-sided claim, with no independent verification. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Retaking Bab al-Mandab and the west coast is a top priority that will not be delayed, a government commander says

reports.text: Point-blank fighting broke out at Al-Sudayr, a border front in Lahj, between Al-Subayhah tribesmen and Houthi forces after an attempt to infiltrate tribal positions. Field sources say the battle is continuing, that Houthi forces took casualties, without giving figures, and that the tribesmen hold the situation. This is a local claim, with no independent verification. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Point-blank fighting at Al-Sudayr in Lahj between Al-Subayhah tribesmen and Houthi forces after an infiltration attempt
Residents of Al-Mashariqah in Al-Shamayatayn claim they foiled a Houthi infiltration, with two local people and one Houthi fighter killed
reports.text: Residents and local young men in the Al-Mashariqah area of Al-Shamayatayn district in south-eastern Taiz say they foiled an infiltration by Houthi fighters who, according to the account, had fled the Al-Ahkum front and lost their way before reaching Al-Mashariqah at dawn. Clashes broke out in which two local men and one of the infiltrators were killed. Security forces cordoned off the area to search it and, according to the same account, detained the rest of the group. This is a government-aligned local source, with no independent verification. Al-Muntasaf carried the account.

Houthi forces tried to advance towards Sharirah in Al-Wazi'iyah in western Taiz and briefly held several sites, before Al-Alqamah fighters mounted a broad counter-attack that recovered the positions and pushed the Houthis back from Sharirah towards Bilad al-Dharifah. Three local fighters were wounded, one seriously, and evacuated to Aden. Tribal sources say the local command is under Brigadier General Abu Dhiab al-Alqami. This is a local claim, with no independent verification. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Houthi forces tried to advance towards Sharirah in Al-Wazi'iyah and briefly held several sites

reports.text: Nasr Taha Mustafa, adviser to the chairman of the Presidential Leadership Council, attributed the fall of Mocha to the Houthi decision to end the 2022 truce and open a full war, timed with the Iran-US tension over Hormuz. He said the breach at the Khalid bin al-Walid camp threatened to encircle government and National Resistance forces at Hays and Al-Khokha and forced a withdrawal south, and claimed more than 2,000 Houthi fighters were killed in the fighting, a figure that has not been verified. He described Houthi control of the coast and the port as temporary and warned against wider open campaigns. Almashhad carried the account, citing Al Jazeera Net.
reports.summary: Nasr Taha Mustafa, adviser to the chairman of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, blames the fall of Mocha on the Houthi decision to end the truce

reports.text: At least 112,000 people have been displaced inside Yemen in the past two weeks, revised up from about 104,800 on 16 September, and some 3,000 have crossed by sea to Djibouti in under a week. The Djiboutian government is preparing for up to 10,000 refugees. The IOM describes overloaded boats with limited food and water, carrying mostly Yemeni families along with a small number of Ethiopian migrants. UNHCR also notes a slight rise in arrivals in Somaliland and Puntland, in the hundreds. Reuters and Arab News reported from Geneva.
reports.summary: At least 112,000 internally displaced in Yemen over two weeks, revised up from about 104,800 on 16 September

reports.text: Abdul Wahid Abu Ras, deputy foreign minister in the Houthi administration in Sanaa, gave the first Houthi-attributed response to the US State Department's approval of a possible sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia, worth about $24.3 billion, saying it exposes the American role in the offensive against Yemen. The package also covers 49 Pratt & Whitney engines. Washington says it does not alter the regional balance of power. The sale still requires congressional approval. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Abdul Wahid Abu Ras, deputy foreign minister in the Houthi administration in Sanaa, gives the first Houthi-attributed response

reports.text: The government army says it broke into several Houthi positions at Aghbara, at the edge of Al-Wazi'iyah in western Taiz, after a surprise attack, and that fighting is continuing with further gains claimed. Separately, Al-Khulasa reported that Giants Brigades units blocked a Houthi attack launched overnight on Thursday and recovered positions lost in the same area, claiming dozens of Houthi fighters killed. These are local and government claims, with no independent verification. This location in western Taiz is distinct from the Al-Aghbara front in Lahj. Almashhad carried the account.
reports.summary: Government claims of an advance at Aghbara in western Taiz after fighting with Houthi forces
Italian defence minister says an Italian Eurofighter F-2000 was damaged in a strike on Taif air base in Saudi Arabia, with no Italian casualties
reports.text: Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto confirmed that an Italian F-2000 Eurofighter was damaged in a strike on King Fahd air base at Taif in western Saudi Arabia overnight on Thursday. He said he followed the incident directly with the chief of the defence staff, General Luciano Portolano. An Italian contingent is stationed there under Operation Inherent Resolve. No Italian personnel were hurt, the aircraft was parked in a peripheral area of the base, and no other equipment or infrastructure used by the Italian force was damaged. The extent of the damage to the aircraft was not disclosed. The Aviationist and other outlets link the strike to a wave of Houthi launches at targets in Saudi Arabia, an attribution Crosetto did not make explicitly, and note that about four Eurofighters have been deployed with Task Force Air – Arabia since March 2026. This is the first known report of a European fighter aircraft damaged in the current round. ANSA reported the account.

A Houthi drone hit the al-Makhlafi family at Hays, south of Hodeidah, as they were trying to leave the fighting. Four were killed: a woman eight months pregnant, her husband, her husband's mother and a two-year-old child. Local sources link the incident to the wave of people leaving after the Houthi advance between Hays and Mocha. Almashhad carried it.
reports.summary: Houthi drone hit the al-Makhlafi family at Hays, south of Hodeidah, as they tried to flee the fighting

reports.text: Fighting on the Kahbub heights in Lahj, facing Bab al-Mandab, has been fluid since Wednesday, with high ground changing hands in counter-attacks and no decisive breakthrough. Government sources report at least 19 killed and 15 wounded, most by Houthi missiles, with casualties evacuated to Aden. Houthi sources report at least 25 killed and further wounded, with evacuation difficult under air cover. Taken together the two sides account for more than 40 dead in 24 hours. The figures sit awkwardly with the claim of full control of the heights, and this desk's control map stays unchanged. Xinhua and China Daily carried the accounts from military sources on both sides.
reports.summary: Fluid fighting on the Kahbub heights in Lahj facing Bab al-Mandab, with high ground changing hands in counter-attacks and no decisive breakthrough

reports.text: Yahya Saree, the Houthi military spokesman, said on X that 37 Saudi F-15 sorties flown from Khamis Mushait air base struck Taiz and Hajjah over 24 hours and caused civilian casualties. He gave no casualty figures, and there is no independent Saudi confirmation. Xinhua and China Daily carried the claim.
reports.summary: Saree claims 37 Saudi F-15 sorties from Khamis Mushait air base struck Taiz and Hajjah

reports.text: Saada's governor, Major General Turki Ahmed Muzhir bin Qamsha, accused the Houthis of turning the governorate into a centre for running wars and a threat to neighbouring states, holy sites and international shipping. He said the people of Saada condemn attempts to strike Mecca and Saudi Arabia, and that the Houthis do not represent Saada or Yemen. Aden Observer carried the remarks, citing Okaz.
reports.summary: Saada governor Major General Turki Ahmed Muzhir bin Qamsha accuses the Houthis of turning Saada into a war command centre
Government army, via Anadolu, claims 30 Houthi fighters killed and 60 wounded in 24 hours in Al-Wazi'iyah, alongside air strikes on supply routes at Mocha
reports.text: A military source at the armed forces media centre said 30 Houthi fighters were killed and more than 60 wounded in fighting and air strikes in Al-Wazi'iyah district in western Taiz, around the Al-Dharifah junction. Government aircraft also struck supply routes at Mocha. This is a one-sided claim, with no independent confirmation. Anadolu and Saudi Gazette carried it.

Harith Lutf al-Azi, once described as an Ansar al-Sharia emir in Taiz, was killed in a road accident described as mysterious in the Asr area west of Sanaa, after reports that he had joined the Houthis. The circumstances have not been verified beyond the local report. Almashhad carried it.
reports.summary: Harith Lutf al-Azi, once named an Ansar al-Sharia emir in Taiz, killed in a road accident described as mysterious

reports.text: Rahim Safavi, senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader on armed forces affairs, praised the Houthi advance on the west coast and their arrival at Bab al-Mandab as a blessed victory, and said the Houthis had broken what he called the myth of an undefeated America from Sanaa to the strait. This is an Iranian statement of support, not an independent battlefield account. Almashhad carried it, citing IRNA.
reports.summary: Rahim Safavi, senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader on armed forces affairs, praises the Houthi advance on the west coast
Arab News reports a fourth consecutive day of battle for the Kahbub heights in Lahj facing Bab al-Mandab, with a government official saying the Houthis made no gains
reports.text: Heavy fighting continued on Thursday, the fourth consecutive day, around a strategic hill at Madaribah and Al-Arah overlooking Bab al-Mandab. A Yemeni government official close to the front told Arab News that the Houthis had thrown heavy attacks at government forces on the Kahbub heights but had so far failed to advance, and that the fighting was intensifying at Madaribah. The army said air strikes hit Houthi reinforcements south-east of Taiz and along the Al-Barh to Mocha road, and blocked an attack at Jabal Habashi in western Taiz. Rashad al-Alimi, chairman of the Presidential Leadership Council, said the Houthis had taken heavy losses in Taiz, Marib, Lahj, Al-Jawf, Hajjah, Al-Bayda and Al-Dhale. Saeed al-Batati reported from Mukalla for Arab News.

Gunfire, explosions and Houthi air defence fire were heard across Sanaa into the morning. Aden Observer described concentrations at Sawan and Al-Hasabah between about 04:30 and 05:00, followed by explosions around 05:00. Houthi-aligned accounts described air defences engaging drones over the city, while Khabar quoted local sources claiming government aircraft were overhead. Rumours that a senior financial figure was killed, or of an internal dispute at Al-Hasabah, are unverified. Neither the Houthi authorities nor the government issued a statement, and the nature of the incident remains unclear. Almashhad, Aden Observer and Khabar carried local accounts.
reports.summary: Gunfire, explosions and Houthi air defence fire heard in Sanaa into the morning
AFP reports 68 killed in 24 hours: 23 government soldiers in two south-western districts and 40 Houthi fighters, according to Houthi sources, in air and ground attacks
reports.text: A government official told AFP that at least 23 soldiers were killed in Houthi missile and drone attacks in two districts of south-western Yemen. Houthi military sources reported 40 killed in Saudi air strikes and ground fighting. The combined figure of 68 is the sum of claims from both sides, not an independent count.

Houthi authorities detained senior field commanders on the west coast on accusations of spying for government forces, confiscating phones for security and intelligence checks, according to sources. The men are said to be held in military buildings at Mocha, with families told they were attending cultural or training courses rather than being detained. Almashhad carried it.
reports.summary: Houthis detain senior field commanders on the west coast on charges of spying for government forces

reports.text: The National Commission of Inquiry into human rights violations recorded 2,062 incidents with 2,932 casualties between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026, out of 35,015 since 2016. They include 501 cases of civilians killed or wounded — 193 dead, among them 30 children and 15 women, and 388 wounded — of which 446 are attributed to the Houthis, 31 to government forces and 24 to others. The report also lists 57 allegations of recruiting children under 18, 56 of them against the Houthis, along with 112 mine explosions causing 120 casualties, 534 arbitrary detentions or disappearances, 371 of them by the Houthis, and 55 documented cases of forced displacement. The commission is a government body and the figures have no independent international verification.
reports.source: Barran Press · Yemen Monitor · National Investigation Commission
reports.summary: 2,062 violation incidents with 2,932 casualties documented between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026, out of 35,015 recorded since 2016

reports.text: The UN human rights office verified 55 civilian casualties in 19 incidents in Taiz, Hodeidah, Marib and Lahj since the start of September, 84% of them women and children, and said the real number is probably higher. OCHA said access and funding are holding back the response: 15,000 emergency kits are ready but most cannot be delivered because roads are closed, the port of Mocha is shut after damage, and the WFP reports disruption at 17 distribution points. CERF released $9 million on Tuesday, and the 2026 emergency plan is only about 20% funded. Both agencies called for protection of civilians and humanitarian access. Xinhua carried the briefing.
reports.summary: UN human rights office verifies 55 civilian casualties in 19 incidents in Taiz, Hodeidah, Marib and Lahj since the start of September

reports.text: Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, army chief Asim Munir and ISI head Asim Malik in Islamabad to discuss Yemen, Saudi Arabia and the risk of the conflict widening. Turkey's defence ministry condemned Houthi drone attacks on Saudi Arabia and stressed formalising the Mecca pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan as a collective defence arrangement. Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said it was time to activate the pact and that he had passed Tehran a Saudi message about concern over Houthi attacks. Barran Press and Anadolu carried the account.
reports.summary: Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin meets Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir in Islamabad

reports.text: In its first statement on the Red Sea escalation, the African Union Commission condemned Houthi attacks on civilian targets and infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and attacks and threats against commercial shipping. It said it was particularly concerned by reports of attempts to strike Mecca and the holy cities, stressed freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and at Bab al-Mandab under international law, and warned that disruption to the passage harms African economies, global trade and energy supply. It called for an immediate halt to attacks, de-escalation and dialogue. Yemen Monitor carried the statement.
reports.summary: European Union takes its first position on the escalation in the Red Sea
Damage to the East-West pipeline exposes the limits of Saudi Arabia's alternative export routes
reports.text: Saudi Arabia halted exports from Yanbu after drone strikes on pumping stations along the East-West pipeline on 10 September. Part of the flow has already been rerouted north through the Suez Canal, which is more expensive and slower for Asian markets. AGSI reported the account.

A military source on the Taiz axis claimed 30 Houthi fighters were killed and more than 60 wounded over 24 hours in Al-Wazi'iyah district in western Taiz, mainly around the Al-Dharifah junction, along with six combat vehicles and two tanks destroyed. Government air strikes hit troop concentrations and vehicles in the same area. This is a one-sided claim, with no independent verification. Okaz carried it.
reports.summary: Fighting over the past 24 hours in Al-Wazi'iyah district in western Taiz, mainly around the Al-Dharifah junction

reports.text: Trump administration approves a possible sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia at an estimated $24.3 billion on 18 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.source: Al Jazeera · AFP · US State Department · Reuters
reports.summary: Trump administration approves a possible sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia at an estimated $24.3 billion

reports.text: UN food agency scales up its emergency response after about 125,000 people were displaced on the west coast on 18 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: UN food agency scales up its emergency response after about 125,000 people were displaced on the west coast
Fierce clashes and air strikes leave casualties in Al-Wazi'iyah
reports.text: AL-WAZI'IYAH — Clashes and air strikes targeting Houthi forces in Al-Wazi'iyah district west of Taiz resulted in 90 casualties.
Saudi Arabia offered the Houthis a two-week truce through Oman, with direct talks on humanitarian demands on 18 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Saudi Arabia offered the Houthis a two-week truce through Oman, with direct talks on humanitarian demands

reports.text: Pakistani army spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry says Pakistan will defend Saudi Arabia on 18 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Pakistani army spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry says Pakistan will defend Saudi Arabia

reports.text: Qatar strongly condemns the Houthi drone attack on Taif, which killed a Yemeni resident and wounded two people on 18 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Qatar strongly condemns the Houthi drone attack on Taif, which killed a Yemeni resident and wounded two people

reports.text: Strong condemnation of the drone attack on Taif, which killed a Yemeni resident and left a Saudi woman wounded and a Pakistani man critically injured on 18 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Strong condemnation of the drone attack on Taif, which killed a Yemeni resident and left a Saudi woman wounded and a Pakistani man critically injured

reports.text: Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi condemns the Houthi drone attack on Taif on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi condemns the Houthi drone attack on Taif

reports.text: Dozens of fighters from the Saudi-backed Sixth Military Region stage an armed protest in central Marib after their names were struck from the payroll on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Dozens of fighters from the Saudi-backed Sixth Military Region stage an armed protest in central Marib after their names were struck from the payroll

reports.text: Claims of widespread looting by Houthi forces in the Second of December housing compound in Mocha, with dozens of flats broken into on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Claims of widespread looting by Houthi forces in the Second of December housing compound in Mocha, with dozens of flats broken into

reports.text: Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto orders the navy to prepare to escort Italian merchant ships through Bab al-Mandab on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto orders the navy to prepare to escort Italian merchant ships through Bab al-Mandab

reports.text: Kuwait and Bahrain separately condemn the Houthi drone intercepted over Taif on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Kuwait and Bahrain separately condemn the Houthi drone intercepted over Taif

reports.text: EU foreign policy spokesman Anouar El Anouni condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: EU foreign policy spokesman Anouar El Anouni condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia

reports.text: Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir calls Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and urges Tehran to rein in the Houthis on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir calls Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and urges Tehran to rein in the Houthis
Yemeni warplanes target Houthi reinforcements on Al-Barh road
reports.text: AL-BARH — Yemeni military warplanes carried out intensive air strikes targeting Houthi reinforcements and gatherings along the Al-Barh - Al-Wazi'iyah road.

Condemnation of any attack on Islamic holy sites, notably Mecca, Medina and Al-Aqsa, while stressing that the drone interception remains only a claim on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Condemnation of any attack on Islamic holy sites, notably Mecca, Medina and Al-Aqsa, while stressing that the drone interception remains only a claim
UKMTO reports small boat approach oil tanker east of Aden
reports.text: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that an oil tanker was approached by a small boat trying to intercept its course 75 nautical miles east of Aden.

reports.summary: Saree: Saudi jets launched 37 air strikes over 24 hours
reports.text: TAIZ — Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree stated that Saudi warplanes carried out 37 F-15 air strikes taking off from Khamis Mushait Air Base against Taiz and Hajjah governorates.
Houthi video of Saudi fighter-jet wreckage geolocated on 17 September. Full detail is at the source link.
reports.summary: Houthi video of Saudi fighter-jet wreckage geolocated

events.text: JEDDAH — The Saudi-led multinational defensive naval coalition held its fourth planning session at Western Fleet headquarters in Jeddah, attended by 154 naval commanders, planners, ambassadors and European Union representatives from 41 states, the Saudi defence ministry said. The coalition has reached initial operational capability and moved from formation to integrating capabilities, operational readiness and a physical presence in the maritime area it covers, with 28 liaison officers. Its stated aim is to protect freedom of navigation, sea lanes and straits under international law. No deployment timetable was given, the 41 states were not named, and the statement makes no explicit reference to Yemen or Bab al-Mandab. This is a diplomatic announcement, not a change of control.
events.source: Saudi Gazette · Al Arabiya · Saudi MoD
events.label: Jeddah — naval coalition reaches initial capability, 41 states

events.text: Three children were killed in the village of Al-Tarirah in Al-Wazi'iyah district in western Taiz, in what local sources describe as Houthi shelling of a residential area. The names published were Nur al-Din Yaqub Abduh al-Tharafi, about four; Asawar Fahd Mohammed Ghanim al-Tharafi, 14; and Tala Mohammed Ahmed al-Tharafi, about two. The sources link the incident to the escalation in western Taiz and to shelling of inhabited areas. An earlier Al Jazeera and AFP report on 17 September carried a separate Houthi media claim blaming government and coalition forces for the same village, leaving the attribution contested. Almashhad and Saba carried the accounts.

events.text: AL-KADHA — Government forces and the Popular Resistance in western Taiz say they foiled a Houthi attack on the Al-Kadha front, shot down two Houthi drones before they reached their targets and killed 15 of the attackers. events.text: Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto confirmed that an Italian F-2000 Eurofighter was damaged in a strike on King Fahd air base at Taif in western Saudi Arabia overnight on Thursday. He said he followed the incident directly with the chief of the defence staff, General Luciano Portolano. An Italian contingent is stationed there under Operation Inherent Resolve. No Italian personnel were hurt, the aircraft was parked in a peripheral area of the base, and no other equipment or infrastructure used by the Italian force was damaged. The extent of the damage to the aircraft was not disclosed. The Aviationist and other outlets link the strike to a wave of Houthi launches at targets in Saudi Arabia, an attribution Crosetto did not make explicitly, and note that about four Eurofighters have been deployed with Task Force Air – Arabia since March 2026. This is the first known report of a European fighter aircraft damaged in the current round. ANSA reported the account.
events.label: Taif — Italian Eurofighter damaged in a strike, Crosetto says

timeline.title: Roots of the Houthi movement
timeline.summary: In northern Yemen, around Saada, a Zaydi religious and social movement grew up around the al-Houthi family — the root of what later became the Houthis.
timeline.detail: Unified Yemen was created in 1990 from the merger of north and south. In the far northern highlands, and especially in Saada governorate on the Saudi border, Zaydi communities — a Shia tradition particular to Yemen — felt pushed aside by the centre in Sanaa. Hussein Badreddin al-Houthi led study circles and activism known as the Believing Youth: at first a religious and social identity rather than a national army. Poverty in the north, President Ali Abdullah Saleh's suspicion of the movement, and regional tensions after 2003 gradually turned it into an armed political force. This period is the foundation of today's Houthi movement.
timeline.mapNote: The focus is Saada and the northern highlands — still far from Sanaa and the coast.

timeline.title: The Saada wars
timeline.summary: Between 2004 and 2010 Yemeni government forces fought the Houthis in Saada through six rounds. Hussein al-Houthi was killed, but the movement survived and grew stronger.
timeline.detail: The first round broke out in 2004 after Saleh's government tried to detain Hussein al-Houthi. He was killed that year — and rather than dissolving the movement, his death consolidated it around his brothers and tribal allies. Six rounds of fighting followed, at times drawing in Saudi forces on the border. Neither side won outright: the Houthis learned to fight, built local networks and accumulated weapons and experience. The political wound in the north never closed, so when the state faltered in 2011 they were no longer merely local rebels.
timeline.mapNote: Fighting concentrated in and around Saada — not yet a war for all of Yemen.

timeline.title: The Arab Spring and Saleh's fall
timeline.summary: The 2011 protests weakened Saleh's rule. He was replaced by Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi, and the Houthis used the vacuum to expand south from Saada.
timeline.detail: As in other Arab states, crowds turned out in Yemen against a long-serving ruler. Saleh was pushed into a negotiated exit brokered by the Gulf states, and the interim president, Hadi, tried to run a national dialogue and write a new constitution. In practice the army and the state split, security weakened, and groups such as al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula exploited the chaos. The Houthis, already hardened by the Saada wars, pushed south, took more ground in the north, and at times cooperated with remnants of Saleh's camp. This is the point at which they stopped being a local story and became a national actor.
timeline.mapNote: Gradual expansion south from Saada towards Sanaa.

timeline.title: The fall of Sanaa
timeline.summary: In September 2014 the Houthis took Sanaa. The government collapsed, Hadi fled, and Yemen entered full national war.
timeline.detail: After capturing Amran to the north of the capital, Houthi fighters entered Sanaa, partly backed by forces tied to Saleh, who wanted revenge on the system that removed him. They seized ministries, weapons and institutions. UN-brokered agreements did not hold. In February 2015 Hadi fled first to Aden and then to Saudi Arabia. From this point there were in effect two Yemens: a Houthi-held north-west with Sanaa as its de facto capital, and a government and southern camp reliant on outside support. That fracture line runs through to today's map.
timeline.mapNote: The north-west passes to Houthi control, with the capital in their hands.

timeline.title: The Saudi-led intervention
timeline.summary: In March 2015 a Saudi-led coalition opened an air campaign to restore Hadi's government — the start of the regional war over Yemen.
timeline.detail: Saudi Arabia and its allies feared Houthi control, seen as close to Iran, over their southern border and over sea lanes. The campaign, named Decisive Storm and then Restoring Hope, combined air strikes, a partial naval blockade and support for local forces in the south. Aden was taken back from the Houthis in 2015 and became the seat of the internationally recognised government — but Sanaa and most of the north-west stayed in Houthi hands. Instead of a quick decision, a long war of attrition opened, at very heavy civilian cost.
timeline.mapNote: The south returns to the government; the north-west stays Houthi.

timeline.title: Fixed fronts: Taiz, Marib and the south
timeline.summary: Years of relative stalemate: Taiz under partial siege, Marib a government energy stronghold, and a widening split in the south between the government and separatist forces.
timeline.detail: The front lines set. Taiz — a large city in south-western Yemen between the highlands and the coast — became a symbol of civilian suffering, with fighting, partial siege and difficult aid access. Marib in the east stayed important for its oil and gas and its government administration. In the south the Southern Transitional Council emerged, a separatist force seeking an independent or autonomous south, which at times fought Hadi's government as well as the Houthis. The anti-Houthi camp was never a single ordered bloc.
timeline.mapNote: Front lines harden; the south is politically split.

timeline.title: The Stockholm Agreement and Hodeidah
timeline.summary: In late 2018 a UN-brokered agreement covered the port of Hodeidah, to head off a major battle over Yemen's humanitarian import artery.
timeline.detail: Hodeidah is the main Red Sea port; food, fuel and aid for much of the population come through it. Coalition and government forces were closing on the port and the UN warned of humanitarian catastrophe. In December 2018, at talks in Sweden, the parties agreed a local ceasefire, a redeployment around the port and a monitoring mechanism, along with a prisoner exchange and understandings on Taiz. Implementation was partial and cumbersome — but the big battle for the port was averted. The west coast stayed fragile from then on, even as fighting continued elsewhere.
timeline.mapNote: The west coast is relatively frozen around the port — not a national peace.

timeline.title: The 2022 truce and the Presidential Council
timeline.summary: A UN-brokered truce in April 2022 slowed the fighting, and a Presidential Leadership Council replaced Hadi.
timeline.detail: The truce cut air strikes and temporarily opened routes to the ports and the airport — real relief for civilians, without ending the war. In parallel Hadi handed his powers to a Presidential Leadership Council under Rashad al-Alimi, an attempt to unify the anti-Houthi camp under a collective leadership recognised internationally as Yemen's legitimate government. The truce eroded and never became a permanent peace, but it changed the tempo: less daily escalation, until broader fighting resumed in the years that followed.
timeline.mapNote: Fighting slows, with no major change of control on the map.

timeline.title: The Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab
timeline.summary: From late 2023 the Houthis attacked shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab strait, and the US, Britain and partners answered with strikes and naval operations.
timeline.detail: After the war in Gaza began, the Houthis declared attacks on vessels they said were linked to Israel or its allies. In practice global trade routes through the Bab al-Mandab strait — the chokepoint between the Red Sea and the Arabian Sea — were disrupted. Shipping lines rerouted around Africa and freight rates rose. The US and Britain led military responses and maritime protection operations. Yemen's internal conflict connected to a regional and global front. Bab al-Mandab and the west coast are an international corridor, not only a Yemeni border.
timeline.mapNote: The focus shifts to the sea, at Bab al-Mandab and in the Red Sea.

timeline.title: Realignment in the south before the 2026 round
timeline.summary: In early 2026 a political and military reshuffle in the south narrowed the split between separatist forces and the Presidential Council, in preparation for renewed fighting in the west.
timeline.detail: Years of friction between the Southern Transitional Council and the government had weakened the ability to face the Houthis on a single front. Open-source reporting from early 2026 described separatist structures being dissolved or reintegrated and realigned under the Presidential Council in Aden, alongside reinforcements and coordination. This was not peace in the south, but an attempt to stop fighting each other before the big round on the coast. Both sides therefore entered the September 2026 escalation in the west better prepared.
timeline.mapNote: The south is more aligned against the coastal front — still no decision.

timeline.title: September 2026: the Red Sea coast, and the present
timeline.summary: In September 2026 the Houthis broke back onto the west coast, took the port city of Mocha and closed on the Bab al-Mandab strait, while fighting continued in western Taiz and Lahj and mass displacement spread from the coast.
timeline.detail: After years of relative stalemate since the 2022 truce, a broad round of fighting opened on the Red Sea coast. Houthi forces advanced south and captured Mocha, a port city in south-western Yemen, then reported further progress towards Bab al-Mandab and a presence on sensitive islands including Mayun and Hanish, though some of those reports remain disputed or only partly verified. Control of the coast and of the approaches to the strait affects international shipping and the government's ability to hold the country's south-west. Government forces and tribal allies counter-attacked around Al-Wazi'iyah in western Taiz, near Hays and in Lahj, and tried to halt the advance. Pressure continued around Marib, the energy stronghold in the east, alongside fire and launches tied to Saudi Arabia and to the sea. UN agencies reported tens and then hundreds of thousands displaced from the west coast. The coast and the strait are the heart of the current round.
timeline.mapNote: The west coast, Bab al-Mandab, Taiz, Lahj and Marib.

fronts.name: Bab al-Mandab and the south-west coast
fronts.where: The Bab al-Mandab strait in south-western Yemen, between the Red Sea and the Arabian Sea
fronts.plain: Ships pass here between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. Mayun and Hanish are in Houthi hands; the high ground facing them in Lahj, on the Kahbub heights, is an open battle.
fronts.summary: A fourth consecutive day of fighting for the Kahbub heights in Lahj, which overlook the strait. Arab News, citing a government official, says the Houthis made no gains. The islands and the coast facing the strait remain in Houthi hands according to reporting from mid-September.
fronts.detail: Houthi forces hold Mocha, Dhubab, Mayun and Hanish according to reporting from 11 and 12 September. Fighting continues on the Kahbub heights, at Madaribah and Al-Arah: Xinhua reported high ground changing hands and more than 40 killed on 17 September, citing sources on both sides, while Arab News on 18 September quoted a government official saying the militia had not advanced by a centimetre. There is no verified change of control in the strait itself. UKMTO says the maritime threat remains focused on vessels with a Saudi connection.

fronts.name: Red Sea coast (Mocha to Dhubab)
fronts.where: The Red Sea coastal strip in south-western Yemen
fronts.plain: The corridor that connects the interior to the coast. Mocha's fall opened the road south towards the strait.
fronts.detail: The fall of Mocha on 10 September was the turning point of this round: from there the axis opened south to Dhubab and Mayun. Air strikes on supply routes between Al-Wazi'iyah and Mocha have been reported since, without the government claiming any re-entry into the port city.

fronts.name: Western Taiz and Al-Wazi'iyah
fronts.where: The districts between Taiz city and the Red Sea coast
fronts.plain: The fight here is over the corridor linking the interior to the coast. The ground is mixed — neither side holds all of it.
fronts.summary: The government army, via Al Jazeera on 18 September, repeats a claim of 30 Houthi fighters killed and 60 wounded in Al-Wazi'iyah in 24 hours, around the Al-Dharifah junction. It is a one-sided claim, with no verified change to the line.
fronts.detail: Local reporting describes an attack blocked at Al-Kadha and drones shot down, and three children killed at Al-Tarirah, with attribution disputed between sources. This is the connecting front: whoever holds it links or cuts Taiz city from the coast at Mocha.

fronts.name: Marib
fronts.where: Eastern Yemen — an oil and gas city
fronts.plain: The city and the main district are government-held. Houthi pressure comes from the west, with no change of control.
fronts.summary: Al Jazeera, 18 September: a claim of combined sniper and artillery fire against a crew and a 106mm gun in the west of the governorate — a one-sided claim. BBC Verify documented F-15 wreckage west of the city.

fronts.name: Al-Dhale
fronts.where: The southern highlands of Yemen, north-west of Aden
fronts.plain: Anadolu reported a Houthi drone shot down on the Murays front. No ground battle has changed control here.

fronts.name: Al-Jawf and Al-Hazm
fronts.where: North-eastern Yemen, close to the Saudi border
fronts.plain: The Houthis hold the governorate capital, Al-Hazm. Government forces are pressing from the desert through the Al-Lubanat camp, with no verified decision.
fronts.summary: Al-Araby, 16 September: government forces claim control of the desert half of the Al-Lubanat camp, while the hill section remains Houthi-held. Al-Hazm itself has not fallen.
fronts.detail: Control of the camp would open a corridor of about 50km to Al-Hazm, held by the Houthis since 2020. There is no independent confirmation that the governorate capital has fallen. This is a secondary front beside the Saudi border, running alongside the pressure on Marib.

recentDigests.title: Overnight 18-19 September: Riyadh, Azal, Syria
recentDigests.text: First air defence alerts in Riyadh and Al-Kharj, with explosions in Olaya. An explosion at a Houthi security compound in Azal killed four according to local sources, and Saree blamed Saudi Arabia without giving detail. Al-Akhbar reported that Syria turned down a Saudi request for fighters.

recentDigests.title: Evening of 18 September: Kahbub, ICG, UNHCR and WHO
recentDigests.text: Al Jazeera: a claimed attack blocked at Kahbub and a drone downed at Rajum. Crisis Group calls for a pause. UNHCR counts about 3,000 arrivals in Djibouti; WHO finds 60% of health facilities functioning. UKMTO reports no new attack on shipping today.

recentDigests.title: 18 September: Al-Sudayr, new artillery, IOM at 112,000
recentDigests.text: A claim of point-blank fighting at Al-Sudayr in Lahj; a government source describes the Jahannam and Al-Aqrab systems and a priority on Bab al-Mandab; the IOM counts at least 112,000 displaced and about 3,000 arrivals in Djibouti.

recentDigests.title: Overnight 14-15 September: western Marib, Al-Suwayda, Kahbub, IOM at 94,000
recentDigests.text: A claimed roadside bomb foiled west of Marib; missiles near the Al-Suwayda camp; entrenchment on the Kahbub heights; a Tihama force formed under Tareq Saleh; the IOM counts about 94,000 displaced.

situation.summary: Active war with no decisive outcome. Air defence alerts were sounded overnight in Riyadh and Al-Kharj for the first time, with explosions heard in Olaya. In Sanaa, an explosion hit a Houthi security compound in Azal, and Saree blamed Saudi Arabia without giving detail. Fighting continues in Taiz, Lahj and Marib.
